* #48026
* #48025
* #48024

* #48003
* #48002
* #48001

## Motivation

The unified memory pool sized its arena from token counts and handled state (Mamba/GDN/KDA recurrent state), request-indexed and fixed payloads in separate, per-model code. This PR makes the KV storage plan declare every payload — state entries, request rows, scratch and derived pages — before allocation, and sizes all of it from one total byte budget, so capacity, resizing and admission read one source.

## Modifications

- Declarations: `mem_cache/kv/decl.py`, `kv/plan.py`, `kv/layout/parts.py`, `kv/memory/fixed.py`, `kv/memory/request_window.py`, `kv/memory/snapshot.py`: state, request, scratch and derived storage are declared parts of the plan; checkpoint and request-reset behavior is preserved through layout views; resume boundaries and tracking effects are carried by the storage.
- Sizing: `mem_cache/kv/sizing.py`, `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `model_executor/pool_configurator.py`: one solve over the total budget sizes FULL, windows and state; every arena band can be resized after capture without changing captured addresses; physical and widened DCP units are accounted separately; request payloads are fitted within the usable budget; runtime sizing includes peak state demand.
- Admission and retraction: `mem_cache/prefill_budget.py`, `managers/schedule_policy.py`, `managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py`: request state-slot demand is shared between sizing and admission; retraction keeps complete entries.
- Linear-attention state staging: `layers/attention/linear/kernels/state_pool_io.py`, `gdn_backend.py`, `gdn_flashinfer.py`, `kda_backend.py`, `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`: with a strided state pool, prefill stages requests' states at rows 1..n and keeps row 0 as the padding row the FlashInfer GDN prefill expects.
- Replay geometry is read only for enabled modes (`fused_recurrent_linear_replayssm.py`, `spec_utils.py`).
- Tests: new declaration, sizing, request-window, state-alignment and staging tests under `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/kv/`, `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/`, plus updates to the existing unified allocator, admission and golden-layout tests.

**Behavior change:** under `--enable-unified-memory`, `--max-total-tokens` sizes the arena (as it sizes separate pools): the arena is the smallest budget whose solve gives that many FULL tokens, with windows and state sized by the same rules. FULL may still grow into the whole arena; the flag is not an allocation cap. Only a pipeline stage's synchronized share caps FULL.

**Known limitation:** with a strided state pool, the GDN prefill path rebuilds its staging indices in every layer. On short-request workloads this costs about 4% (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B TP2 unified, 2x B200, GSM8K 1000 questions, warm server: 36.0 s vs 33.8–35.4 s on `main`). Computing the indices once per forward removes it; the longer-term fix is kernels that take the state slot stride directly.

## Accuracy Tests

Serving validation was run at the **top of this 26-PR stack** (the cumulative change), not at this PR's head. Software: torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GSM8K is few-shot, 500 or 1319 questions as noted; `main` is the same commit the stack is based on, same flags.

| Hardware | Model | Configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, `--enable-unified-memory` (rebased stack) | 0.954 (1319 q) | 0.950–0.954 |
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP1, `--enable-unified-memory --max-total-tokens 120000` (rebased stack) | 0.842 (1319 q) | 0.839 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, MTP (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens) | 0.951, accept length 3.56 | 0.953, 3.56 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, DFlash draft | 0.951, accept length 5.42 | 0.952, 5.44 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PD (prefill TP1 + decode TP1, mooncake), unified, repeated runs | 0.952–0.960, no hang | 0.954–0.958 |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | PD (TP1 + TP1, mooncake), unified | 0.810 | 0.808 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, HiCache | 0.954 | — |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PP2, unified | 0.953 | 0.955 (static pools) |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified (500 q) | 0.958 | 0.960 |
| 2x B200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified, `trtllm_mha` (1319 q) | 0.849 | 0.863 |
| 2x B300 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B / openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified | 0.950 / 0.849 | 0.954 / 0.849 |

On B200 and B300, 40 greedy GSM8K generations were compared with `main`: 35–40 of 40 are identical, and the rest first differ after at least 27 characters (near ties). The H200 runs above other than the two marked "rebased stack" were run at the stack top before it was rebased onto the current base; the code they cover is unchanged by the rebase except for conflict resolutions.

The Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B rows exercise the GDN state staging and state sizing here; the gpt-oss `--max-total-tokens 120000` row exercises the token-limit sizing.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured at the stack top, same flags as `main` (bench_serving, random 4096-in / 512-out unless noted):

| Hardware | Model / configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b, unified, `--max-total-tokens 120000` | 3.93–3.95 req/s | 3.95 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B PD (TP1 + TP1), 2048-in / 256-out | 5.65–6.28 req/s | 6.21–6.29 req/s |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b PD (TP1 + TP1) | 9.39–9.45 req/s | 9.21 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B MTP TP2 / DFlash TP2 | 4.26 / 4.36 req/s | 4.29 / 4.35 req/s |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B TP2 / openai/gpt-oss-120b TP2 | 6.35 / 19.31 req/s | 6.34 / 19.28 req/s |

See the known limitation above for the GDN staging cost on short requests.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+def state_pool_indices(
+    indices: torch.Tensor, *, dtype: torch.dtype = torch.int64
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Tensor extents may outlive their backing; only slot 0 is the padding sink.
+    return indices.clamp_min(0).to(dtype)
+
+
+def gather_pool_states(
+    states: torch.Tensor, indices: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    # Slot 0 is the backed padding sink in both static and unified state pools.
+    safe_indices = state_pool_indices(indices)
+    live_rows = (indices > 0).view(-1, *((1,) * (states.ndim - 1)))
+    return safe_indices, live_rows, torch.where(live_rows, states[safe_indices], 0)
+
+
+def scatter_pool_states(
+    states: torch.Tensor,
+    indices: torch.Tensor,
+    live_rows: torch.Tensor,
+    updates: torch.Tensor,

+    # Every padded lane writes the same zero row, independent of kernel output.
+    states.index_copy_(0, indices, torch.where(live_rows, updates.to(states.dtype), 0))

+"""Typed entry parts with physical row alignment supplied by their consumers."""
+
+import math
+from typing import Mapping, Sequence
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.decl import TensorPartDecl
+
+
+class TensorEntryLayout:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        parts: Sequence[TensorPartDecl],
+        *,
+        row_alignments: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
+    ):
+        self.parts = tuple(parts)
+        if not parts or len({p.name for p in parts}) != len(parts):
+            raise ValueError("an entry requires distinct named parts")
+        row_alignments = {} if row_alignments is None else row_alignments
+        if set(row_alignments) - {p.name for p in parts} or any(
+            alignment <= 0 for alignment in row_alignments.values()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("row alignments must be positive and name entry parts")
+        self.offsets = {}
+        self.layer_strides = {}
+        self.alignment = math.lcm(
+            *(p.dtype.itemsize for p in parts), *row_alignments.values()
+        )
+        offset = 0
+        for part in self.parts:
+            alignment = math.lcm(part.dtype.itemsize, row_alignments.get(part.name, 1))
+            offset = -(-offset // alignment) * alignment
+            self.offsets[part.name] = offset
+            row_bytes = math.prod(part.shape) * part.dtype.itemsize
+            layer_stride = -(-row_bytes // alignment) * alignment
+            self.layer_strides[part.name] = layer_stride
+            offset += (
+                layer_stride * len(part.layer_ids) if part.layer_ids else row_bytes
+            )
+        self.entry_bytes = -(-offset // self.alignment) * self.alignment
+
+    def views(
+        self,
+        raw: torch.Tensor,
+        rows: int,
+        *,
+        entry_bytes: int | None = None,
+        offset_bytes: int = 0,
+    ):
+        stride_bytes = self.entry_bytes if entry_bytes is None else entry_bytes
+        end = offset_bytes + max(0, rows - 1) * stride_bytes + self.entry_bytes
+        if stride_bytes < self.entry_bytes or end > raw.numel():
+            raise ValueError("entry parts exceed their backing")
+        if (
+            stride_bytes % self.alignment
+            or (raw.data_ptr() + offset_bytes) % self.alignment
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("entry stride or base violates its row alignment")
+        views = {}
+        for part in self.parts:
+            itemsize = part.dtype.itemsize
+            if stride_bytes % itemsize or offset_bytes % itemsize:
+                raise ValueError(f"entry stride is not aligned for {part.name!r}")
+            inner_strides = tuple(
+                math.prod(part.shape[i + 1 :]) for i in range(len(part.shape))
+            )
+            strides = (stride_bytes // itemsize, *inner_strides)
+            if part.layer_ids:
+                strides = (self.layer_strides[part.name] // itemsize, *strides)
+            typed = raw[: raw.numel() // itemsize * itemsize].view(part.dtype)
+            views[part.name] = torch.as_strided(
+                typed,
+                size=part.tensor_shape(rows),
+                stride=strides,
+                storage_offset=typed.storage_offset()
+                + (offset_bytes + self.offsets[part.name]) // itemsize,
+            )
+        return views

+"""Stable allocations outside the movable KV chain, owned by its plan."""
+
+import math
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from typing import Sequence
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.decl import TensorPartDecl
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.utils import maybe_init_custom_mem_pool
+from sglang.srt.utils.torch_memory_saver_adapter import TorchMemorySaverAdapter
+
+
+class FixedMemory:
+    """Typed fixed rows allocated before capture, with declaration-driven reset."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        parts: Sequence[TensorPartDecl],
+        *,
+        rows: int,
+        device: str,
+        enable_memory_saver: bool = False,
+    ):
+        self.parts = tuple(parts)
+        if len({p.name for p in parts}) != len(parts):
+            raise ValueError("fixed part names must be unique")
+        if rows < 1:
+            raise ValueError("fixed memory needs the padding row")
+        self.rows = rows
+        self.device = device
+        self.tensors = {}
+        if not self.parts:
+            return
+        adapter = TorchMemorySaverAdapter.create(enable=enable_memory_saver)
+        enabled, pool, _ = maybe_init_custom_mem_pool(device=device)
+        with (
+            adapter.region(GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE),
+            torch.cuda.use_mem_pool(pool) if enabled else nullcontext(),
+        ):
+            for part in self.parts:
+                self.tensors[part.name] = torch.full(
+                    part.tensor_shape(rows),
+                    part.reset_value,
+                    dtype=part.dtype,
+                    device=device,
+                )
+
+    @property
+    def nbytes(self) -> int:
+        return self.rows * sum(part.row_bytes for part in self.parts)
+
+    def reset_rows(self, rows) -> None:
+        if not self.parts:
+            return
+        if not isinstance(rows, torch.Tensor):
+            rows = torch.tensor(rows, dtype=torch.int64)
+        indices = rows.to(device=self.device, dtype=torch.int64, non_blocking=True)
+        for part in self.parts:
+            self.tensors[part.name].index_fill_(
+                part.row_axis, indices, part.reset_value
+            )
+
+    def copy_rows(self, dst: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Snapshot source rows before writing, including overlapping remaps."""
+        for part in self.parts:
+            tensor = self.tensors[part.name]
+            values = tensor.index_select(part.row_axis, src.to(torch.int64))
+            tensor.index_copy_(part.row_axis, dst.to(torch.int64), values)
+
+    def regions(self, parts: Sequence[TensorPartDecl]):
+        """Contiguous fixed rows in stable part-major, then layer order."""
+        from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.storage import Region
+
+        ptrs, lens, items, dims, outer, layers = [], [], [], [], [], []
+        for part in parts:
+            tensor = self.tensors[part.name]
+            views = tensor.unbind(0) if part.layer_ids else (tensor,)
+            layer_ids = part.layer_ids or (-1,)
+            for layer_id, view in zip(layer_ids, views):
+                if view.numel() == 0:
+                    continue
+                assert view.is_contiguous(), "fixed transfer rows must be contiguous"
+                ptrs.append(view.data_ptr())
+                lens.append(view.nbytes)
+                items.append(view[0].nbytes)
+                dims.append(
+                    0 if part.slice_axis is None else part.shape[part.slice_axis]
+                )
+                outer.append(
+                    1
+                    if part.slice_axis is None
+                    else math.prod(part.shape[: part.slice_axis])
+                )
+                layers.append(layer_id)
+        return Region(
+            ptrs=tuple(ptrs),
+            lens=tuple(lens),
+            item_lens=tuple(items),
+            dim_per_tensor=tuple(dims),
+            slice_outer_counts=tuple(outer),
+            layer_ids=tuple(layers),
+        )

+from itertools import product
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch

+class BandSnapshot(msgspec.Struct, kw_only=True):
+    positions: torch.Tensor
+    entries: torch.Tensor

+    page_parts: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}

+class StorageSnapshot(msgspec.Struct, kw_only=True):
+    bands: dict[str, BandSnapshot]
+    request_parts: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+
+
+def _physical(band, indices, *, state):
+    indices = indices.to(torch.int64).reshape(-1)
+    return band.ids.translate(indices) if state else band.ids.translate_write(indices)
+
+
+def _page_positions(indices, page_size):
+    # Remember positions in this request, not its old virtual ids: a restore
+    # may own different virtual pages as well as different physical pages.
+    _, inverse = torch.unique(indices // page_size, sorted=True, return_inverse=True)
+    count = 0 if inverse.numel() == 0 else int(inverse.max().item()) + 1
+    first = torch.full(
+        (count,), indices.numel(), dtype=torch.int64, device=indices.device
+    )
+    return first.scatter_reduce_(
+        0, inverse, torch.arange(indices.numel(), device=indices.device), reduce="amin"
+    )
+
+
+# Retraction runs under memory pressure; a temporary never exceeds this bound.
+# This is a workspace policy, independent of token counts and entry geometry.
+_COPY_CHUNK_BYTES = 16 << 20
+
+
+def _copy_tiles(shape, element_size):
+    remaining = max(1, _COPY_CHUNK_BYTES // element_size)
+    steps = [1] * len(shape)
+    for axis in reversed(range(len(shape))):
+        steps[axis] = max(1, min(shape[axis], remaining))
+        remaining = max(1, remaining // steps[axis])
+    for starts in product(*(range(0, n, step) for n, step in zip(shape, steps))):
+        yield tuple(
+            slice(start, min(start + step, n))
+            for start, step, n in zip(starts, steps, shape)
+        )
+
+
+def _gather_to_cpu(tensor, rows, row_axis):
+    shape = list(tensor.shape)
+    shape[row_axis] = rows.numel()
+    result = torch.empty(shape, dtype=tensor.dtype, device="cpu")
+    for tile in _copy_tiles(shape, tensor.element_size()):
+        source = list(tile)
+        source[row_axis] = slice(None)
+        values = tensor[tuple(source)].index_select(row_axis, rows[tile[row_axis]])
+        result[tile].copy_(values, non_blocking=True)
+    return result
+
+
+def _scatter_from_cpu(tensor, rows, values, value_rows, row_axis):
+    shape = list(values.shape)
+    shape[row_axis] = rows.numel()
+    for tile in _copy_tiles(shape, tensor.element_size()):
+        columns = list(tile)
+        columns[row_axis] = slice(None)
+        source = values[tuple(columns)].index_select(
+            row_axis, value_rows[tile[row_axis]]
+        )
+        tensor[tuple(columns)].index_copy_(
+            row_axis,
+            rows[tile[row_axis]],
+            source.to(tensor.device, non_blocking=True),
+        )
+

+    def test_padded_graph_reads_only_finalized_backing(self):
+        """Padded SM90 replay must not index the unbacked tail of captured state views."""
+        state_spec = MambaSubPoolSpec(
+            name="mamba",
+            layer_num=1,
+            grow_direction="up",
+            conv_state_shapes=((1, 16),),
+            conv_dtype=torch.float32,
+            temporal_state_shape=(1, 128, 128),
+            temporal_dtype=torch.float32,
+        )
+        full_spec = MHASubPoolSpec(
+            name="full",
+            layer_num=1,
+            head_num=1,
+            head_dim=128,
+            store_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            grow_direction="down",
+        )
+        arena = arena_of(
+            [state_spec, full_spec],
+            total_bytes=64 << 20,
+            device="cuda",
+            post_capture_active=True,
+        )
+        states = state_spec.views(arena)[1][0]
+        identity = (states.data_ptr(), tuple(states.shape), tuple(states.stride()))
+        self.assertNotEqual(states.stride(0), states[0].numel())
+        kernel = FlashInferGDNKernel()
+        self.assertFalse(kernel.use_state_pool)
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+        q = torch.randn((1, 3, 1, 128), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        k = torch.randn_like(q)
+        v = torch.randn_like(q)
+        a = torch.zeros((1, 3, 1), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        b = torch.zeros_like(a)
+        A_log = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+        dt_bias = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        indices = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        starts = torch.arange(4, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+        def forward():
+            return kernel.decode(
+                q,
+                k,
+                v,
+                a,
+                b,
+                A_log=A_log,
+                dt_bias=dt_bias,
+                ssm_states=states,
+                cache_indices=indices,
+                query_start_loc=starts,
+            )
+
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            for _ in range(3):
+                forward()
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            output = forward()
+        arena.finalize_backing(4 << 20)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            identity, (states.data_ptr(), tuple(states.shape), tuple(states.stride()))
+        )
+        tail_offset = (
+            states.data_ptr()
+            - arena.raw.data_ptr()
+            + (states.shape[0] - 1) * states.stride(0) * states.element_size()
+        )
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(tail_offset, arena.backed_bytes)
+        states[1:3].copy_(torch.randn_like(states[1:3]) * 0.01)
+        reference = states[:3].clone()
+        for slot in (1, 2, 1):
+            indices.copy_(
+                torch.tensor([slot, -1, -1], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+            )
+            expected = kernel.decode(
+                q[:, :1],
+                k[:, :1],
+                v[:, :1],
+                a[:, :1],
+                b[:, :1],
+                A_log=A_log,
+                dt_bias=dt_bias,
+                ssm_states=reference,
+                cache_indices=indices[:1],
+                query_start_loc=starts[:2],
+            )
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            torch.testing.assert_close(output[:, :1], expected, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                states[1:3], reference[1:3], rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(output[:, 1:]).item(), 0)
+            self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(states[0]).item(), 0)
+        before_idle = states[:3].clone()
+        indices.fill_(-1)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(states[:3], before_idle)
+        self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(output).item(), 0)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+def _strided_pool(rows=8):
+    # A state pool whose slots are strided inside wider entries, as in a unified
+    # arena; slot 0 is the padding sink.
+    envelope = torch.full((rows, 48), 19.0)
+    states = torch.as_strided(envelope, (rows, 1, 4, 4), (48, 16, 4, 1))
+    states[0].fill_(0)
+    for slot in range(1, rows):
+        states[slot].fill_(slot)
+    return states
+
+
+def _extend(kernel, states, indices, num_seqs):
+    qkv = torch.ones((1, num_seqs, 1, 4))
+    gate = torch.zeros((1, num_seqs, 1))
+    with patch(
+        "sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.l2norm.gdn_prefill_qkv_prepare_fwd",
+        side_effect=lambda q, k, v: (q, k, v),
+    ):
+        kernel.extend(
+            qkv,
+            qkv,
+            qkv,
+            gate,
+            gate,
+            ssm_states=states,
+            cache_indices=indices,
+            query_start_loc=torch.arange(num_seqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32),
+        )
+
+
+class TestLinearStateStaging(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_staged_prefill_writes_every_live_request_back(self):
+        """A prefill on contiguous staged copies updates each live request's
+        pool slot, including the request staged first, and leaves padding,
+        the sink and other slots alone."""
+        pool = _strided_pool()
+        conv = _strided_pool()
+        before = pool.clone()
+        indices = torch.tensor([5, 2, -1, 0], dtype=torch.int32)
+
+        (conv_copy, ssm_copy), rows, pool_rows = stage_pool_states(
+            (conv, pool), indices
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(ssm_copy.is_contiguous())
+        _extend(_kernel(), ssm_copy, rows, num_seqs=4)
+        unstage_pool_states((conv, pool), (conv_copy, ssm_copy), pool_rows)
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(pool[5], before[5] + 2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(pool[2], before[2] + 2)
+        for slot in (0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(pool[slot], before[slot])
+        torch.testing.assert_close(conv, _strided_pool())
+
+    def test_zero_based_staging_loses_the_first_request(self):
+        """Why staging keeps the sink at row 0: the kernel treats state index 0
+        as padding, so a request staged at row 0 would get no state."""
+        pool = _strided_pool()
+        copy = pool[torch.tensor([5])].contiguous()
+        _extend(_kernel(), copy, torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int32), num_seqs=1)
+        self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(copy), 0)
+
+

+    unittest.main()

+    def test_token_limit_sizes_the_arena_for_that_many_full_tokens(self):
+        """A token limit sizes the unified arena as the smallest budget whose

+        from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv_cache_configurator import KVCacheConfigurator

+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.dsv41_request_window import RequestWindowSpec
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.memory.request_window import RequestWindowMemory
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import ReqToTokenPool
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci

+
+
+class TestRequestWindowMemory(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_packed_extents_and_fresh_request_row_reset(self):
+        for layout in KVLayout:
+            with self.subTest(layout=layout):
+                spec = RequestWindowSpec.create(
+                    num_slots=4,
+                    layers=2,
+                    page_size=64,
+                    capacity=129,
+                    workspace_rows=513,
+                    kv_layout=layout,
+                )
+                memory = RequestWindowMemory(spec, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cpu")
+                window = memory.view
+                self.assertEqual(spec.capacity, 192)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    memory.nbytes,
+                    2 * 14 * layout.page_bytes(64)
+                    + 2 * 832 * 8
+                    + 10 * layout.page_bytes(64),
+                )
+                window.tags.fill_(19)
+                memory.state.tensors["pages"].fill_(7)
+                table = ReqToTokenPool(3, 16, "cpu", enable_memory_saver=False)
+                table.register_on_alloc_rows(memory.reset_rows)
+                (slot,) = table.alloc_rows(1)
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.all(window.tags[:, slot * 192 : (slot + 1) * 192] == -1)
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(window.tags[:, :192] == 19))
+                # Tags invalidate the packed bytes; acquiring a row need not
+                # clear or move its large payload, nor another request's data.
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(memory.state.tensors["pages"] == 7))
+                window.tags[:, slot * 192 : (slot + 1) * 192].fill_(29)
+                table.free_rows([slot])
+                self.assertEqual(table.alloc_rows(1), [slot])
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.all(window.tags[:, slot * 192 : (slot + 1) * 192] == -1)
+                )
+                expected = torch.tensor(
+                    [slot * 3, slot * 3 + 1, slot * 3 + 2], dtype=torch.int32
+                ).numpy()
+                self.assertTrue((window.page_indices(slot, 0, 192) == expected).all())
+
+    def test_attention_view_preserves_packed_token_dimension(self):
+        """Request-owned packed pages must retain the HIP attention view contract."""
+        for layout in KVLayout:
+            with self.subTest(layout=layout):
+                spec = RequestWindowSpec.create(
+                    num_slots=2,
+                    layers=1,
+                    page_size=64,
+                    capacity=128,
+                    workspace_rows=256,
+                    kv_layout=layout,
+                )
+                memory = RequestWindowMemory(spec, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cpu")
+                for view in (memory.view.state, memory.view.workspace):
+                    packed = view.kv_buffer[0]
+                    attention = packed[:, : 64 * view.kv_cache_total_dim].view(
+                        packed.shape[0], 64, 1, view.kv_cache_total_dim
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(attention.shape[-1], layout.bytes_per_token)
+                    self.assertEqual(attention.data_ptr(), packed.data_ptr())
+
+    def test_activation_cannot_resize_captured_backing(self):
+        spec = RequestWindowSpec.create(
+            num_slots=2,
+            layers=1,
+            page_size=64,
+            capacity=128,
+            workspace_rows=256,
+            kv_layout=KVLayout.V41,
+        )
+        memory = RequestWindowMemory(spec, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cpu")
+        view = memory.view
+        pointer = view.workspace.kv_buffer[0].data_ptr()
+        view.activate(SimpleNamespace(size=256))
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "workspace too small"):
+            view.activate(SimpleNamespace(size=257))
+        self.assertEqual(view.workspace.kv_buffer[0].data_ptr(), pointer)
